- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly in early horizon.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true), especially if sentiment was bullish immediately prior — apply downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.2) triggers lagged overcorrection — model often holds high for 2–3 days after sentiment shift; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day post-reversal.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days (e.g., day 1–5) — dampen initial forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust downward 0.5–1.5% per day until trend stabilizes.
